## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock model discovery could wait indefinitely when the Bedrock control-plane model listing calls stalled, leaving setup and model catalog refresh paths without a bounded failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock discovery now wraps both `ListFoundationModels` and paginated `ListInferenceProfiles` SDK calls in a local 30-second abort deadline using the AWS SDK `client.send(..., { abortSignal })` contract. The existing best-effort fallback remains unchanged: profile discovery failures still degrade to no profiles, and failed foundation discovery still returns an empty discovered catalog.

## User Impact

Users and operators get a bounded Bedrock model discovery failure instead of an indefinitely pending setup or catalog refresh when the AWS control plane stalls. Successful discovery behavior and cached catalog behavior are unchanged.

target.title: fix(tlon): send fragment image URLs as media
target.body:
Related: #104852

AI-assisted PR. I reviewed the diff and focused validation output.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon users sending image media URLs with fragment suffixes, such as `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview`, would have those URLs classified as ordinary links instead of image blocks.

The outbound media story path already treats plain image URLs and image URLs with query strings as image blocks. Fragment-bearing image URLs were the missing sibling case.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change keeps the fix inside Tlon's local image URL classifier by allowing the image extension check to accept either `?query` or `#fragment` suffixes.

This does not change upload behavior, URL fetching, auth, gateway routing, persisted state, migrations, schema, upgrade behavior, or non-image URL handling. It only affects the final Tlon story classification branch for URLs whose path already ends in a known image extension.

## User Impact

Tlon users can now send image URLs that include fragments and still get the expected image media block instead of a plain clickable link when the Tlon send path builds a story from that URL.

For example, `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview` now follows the same media story classification path as `https://cdn.example/image.png` and `https://cdn.example/image.png?token=1`.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the focused local probe showed the mismatch:

```text
https://cdn.example/a.png          => true
https://cdn.example/a.png?token=1  => true
https://cdn.example/a.png#preview  => false
https://cdn.example/a.webp#v=1     => false
```

The focused regression test covers `buildMediaStory("caption", "https://cdn.example/image.png#preview")` and asserts that the URL is emitted as a `block.image` story verse instead of a link verse.

Reviewer-requested live proof is still pending. ClawSweeper asked for redacted evidence from a real Tlon setup showing the upload-fallback path preserves a `.png#fragment` URL and that Tlon renders it as image media. I have not claimed that live proof yet because this machine does not currently have Tlon ship credentials, a login code, or a configured target DM/group channel available.

When a real test setup is available, the intended proof should capture this path:

```text
sendMedia(mediaUrl: "https://[redacted]/image.png#preview")
→ uploadImageFromUrl(mediaUrl)
→ upload fallback returns the original fragment URL
→ buildMediaStory(text, fallbackUrl)
→ Urbit poke payload contains block.image.src
→ Tlon UI renders the message as image media, not a plain link
```

The redacted proof should preserve the `.png#preview` shape and `block.image.src` structure while hiding ship names, login code, cookies, private hosts, request IDs, channel identifiers, and credentials.

## Possible call chain / impact

The relevant source-level fallback chain is:

```text
extensions/tlon/src/channel.runtime.ts sendMedia
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts uploadImageFromUrl
→ on upload failure, return the original imageUrl
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.ts buildMediaStory
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/story.ts isImageUrl
→ createImageBlock or createLinkInline
```

This PR only changes the Tlon-local classifier used by that story-building branch. Sibling behavior for plain image URLs, query-suffixed image URLs, upload success, auth, routing, and non-image URLs is intentionally unchanged.

## Validation

```text
git diff --check
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts
```

Result:

```text

Tests       3 passed (3)
```

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix(searxng): fail closed on unresolved base url refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SearXNG lets users configure `plugins.entries.searxng.config.webSearch.baseUrl` as a SecretRef. When that configured SecretRef could not be resolved locally, runtime resolution could still fall through to the ambient `SEARXNG_BASE_URL` environment variable. That could silently route web_search requests to a different SearXNG host than the explicitly configured one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured credential-like values should either resolve to the configured target or fail closed. This keeps the SearXNG base URL contract aligned with provider-local SecretRef behavior: ambient env fallback is only for the unconfigured case, not for a configured-but-unavailable SecretRef.

## User Impact

Users with a valid configured string or env SecretRef keep the same behavior. Users with no configured baseUrl can still rely on `SEARXNG_BASE_URL`. Users with an unavailable configured SecretRef now get an unavailable SearXNG base URL instead of silently using an unrelated ambient endpoint.

## Evidence

- Added local config matrix coverage for configured string precedence, ambient-env fallback when unconfigured, env SecretRef resolution, missing env SecretRef fail-closed behavior, non-env SecretRef fail-closed behavior, and malformed baseUrl handling.
- Updated `docs/tools/searxng-search.md` so the documented resolution order matches the runtime contract.
- Collision check before edits found no live open PR touching `extensions/searxng/src/config.ts` or the new `extensions/searxng/src/config.test.ts`. Related #104216 touches SearXNG client/provider abort handling, not this config resolver.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

target.title: Instrument native hook relay fan-out
target.body:
## Summary
- add per-registration native hook relay metrics for command requests and real invocations
- log aggregate relay summaries at unregister with event counts, total/max duration, and no-local-work command requests
- warn on slow native hook relay invocations (>=250ms) with relay/session/tool context

## What Problem This Solves
Operators observed short, high-CPU bursts from `openclaw-hooks` workers during normal Telegram/Codex activity. Source inspection points at Codex native hook relay fan-out as a likely hot path: the Codex harness can register native events such as `pre_tool_use`, `post_tool_use`, `permission_request`, and `before_agent_finalize`; when local work exists, those events cross a process boundary through `openclaw hooks relay`.

The important next step is observability, not behavior change. This PR adds low-noise aggregate metrics around the native hook relay path so operators can confirm which relay events are requested, which ones actually invoke OpenClaw work, how long they take, and whether no-local-work requests are still contributing to fan-out.

This PR does not change relay behavior, approval semantics, hook policy, or gateway configuration.

## Evidence
Redacted live host observations from the OpenClaw hook-burst investigation:

- 2026-07-06 hook-cost audit: short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 145-175% CPU during normal Telegram/OpenClaw use, with CPU temperature near 97C in one snapshot. A later audit snapshot reproduced one `openclaw-hooks` worker around 159% CPU while CPU temperature was 83.6C.
- Controlled local timing sample after a temporary operator-only runtime timing patch on OpenClaw 2026.6.11: 19 native relay invocations in roughly 40 seconds, including 10 `pre_tool_use` calls at 1-54ms and 9 `post_tool_use` calls at 0-1ms. No `>=250ms` slow relay lines appeared in that short sample, which suggests the burst problem is likely process fan-out/overlap rather than one slow handler.
- During that same sample, a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker was observed around 163% CPU and disappeared within seconds.
- 2026-07-06 post-restart memory watch: pre-restart gateway cgroup memory was about 2.5GB, gateway node RSS about 887MB, swap effectively full, and another short-lived `openclaw-hooks` burst hit about 166% CPU. Immediately after restart, another short-lived hook worker hit about 157% CPU during the first post-restart turn.
- 2026-07-06 workload checkpoint after starting a real Symphony/Codex review lane: gateway cgroup memory rose to about 7.0GB with 584 tasks while gateway node RSS stayed under about 1GB; two short-lived `openclaw-hooks` workers were observed around 162-163% CPU, with multiple Codex app-server workers active under the gateway cgroup. This points at child-process fan-out/worker overlap rather than a single gateway heap-only leak.
- 2026-07-08 follow-up inspection: gateway cgroup memory was about 5.6GB, cgroup peak about 9.1GB, 417 tasks, swap about 7.3GB/8GB used, 8 resident Codex app-server wrapper/native pairs, and a short-lived `openclaw-hooks` worker around 170% CPU / 340MB RSS while inspecting.

Source-level findings from the same investigation:

- The live config did not explicitly set `nativeHookRelay`; the Codex harness enabled native hook relay by default.
- `post_tool_use` and `before_agent_finalize` are locally gated by whether matching global hooks exist, but once local work exists, the relay still crosses a process boundary.
- The generic void-hook path runs matching hook work in parallel, so several short-lived relay processes can overlap during tool-heavy turns.

## Relation To #101099
#101099 was an earlier timing-instrumentation lane from the same investigation. This PR is the cleaner/narrower aggregate-metrics lane:

- #101099 focused on timing logs from an operator patch direction.
- #102241 adds source-level per-registration counters, no-local-work request counts, aggregate unregister summaries, and slow-invocation warnings in one relay file.

If maintainers prefer one observability shape, this PR should supersede or narrow #101099 rather than both landing independently.

## Verification
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (13/13)
- `TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-native-relay-test-XXXXXX) node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` (80/80)

Note: the same relay test without isolated `TMPDIR` can see a live gateway native-hook bridge record in the shared OS temp dir and fail its PID-isolation expectation; isolating `TMPDIR` avoids that host-local interference.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard direct wiki reads and share supplement registry
target.body:
Related: #101809
Supersedes: #101943

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `memory_get` with `corpus=wiki` would crash the tool run as an unhandled rejection when a registered wiki corpus supplement's `get()` threw (for example config or backend failure), instead of returning a structured disabled error.

Also resolves a problem where Gateway-loaded plugins could register corpus supplements in one module instance while `memory-core` tools read from another empty registry after module reload, so `corpus=wiki` / `corpus=all` lookups could silently miss registered wiki supplements.

## Why This Change Was Made

Guard the direct `corpus=wiki` read path with try-catch and surface the backend failure via `formatErrorMessage()`, matching the structured `{ disabled: true, error }` contract already used for missing wiki results. Store memory plugin supplement state on `globalThis` so Gateway and plugin loaders share one registry across reloads.

Out of scope: supplement search fail-fast (`#77897`, open PR #78035) and the already-merged `corpus=all` fallback guard (#101902).

## User Impact

Agents and operators calling `memory_get corpus=wiki` get a clear disabled error when the wiki backend fails, instead of an unhandled rejection. Wiki/memory corpus supplements remain visible after Gateway plugin reloads.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `3539c7e7653d` (`3539c7e7653da70cbe14fbda89c585f7b925cabe`)

**Unit tests (focused):**

```

✓ shares corpus supplement registry through globalThis across module reloads
```

```

pnpm test src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts -t "globalThis across module reloads"
```

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(ios): block omitted share attachments

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103363.

The iOS Share Extension accepted at most three image attachments and ignored videos, files, PDFs, and unknown attachment providers while still moving toward the normal send flow. That let a user share partial content without any visible explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the current gateway media contract unchanged: the share route still sends image attachments only, and it does not attempt to add video/PDF/file transport in this PR.

Instead, extraction now records selected image count, accepted image count, and unsupported attachment classes. If the extension would omit selected content, the compose card enters the existing blocked state with a concrete recovery message, so send stays disabled until the user removes omitted items and shares again.

## User Impact

- Sharing 6 images now shows: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Sharing a video, PDF/file, or unknown attachment now shows an unsupported-item message instead of silently sending only text or the first accepted images.
- Normal shares with up to 3 images are unchanged.

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires

target.title: feat(tui): opt-in persistence and agent visibility for `!`/`!!` local shell commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

TUI-local `!`-prefixed shell commands render a live local echo but are never persisted: closing the TUI loses them, session resume never shows them, and the agent cannot see what the operator ran or what it printed — even though the `BashExecutionMessage`/`excludeFromContext` data model and the LLM-context filtering for it already exist in `packages/agent-core` (previously unused by any production code path).

Split out of #103147 per review feedback there; that PR now carries only the rendering fixes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Operators often run a `!` command specifically to show the agent something (Claude Code's own `!` behaves this way). But local shell output can also be sensitive, so persistence and model visibility must be a deliberate choice, not a silent default:

- The session consent prompt now offers **No** / **Yes, local only** / **Yes, and share with the agent**. **Local only is the shipped, pre-existing behavior and stays the default expectation** — nothing is saved or shared unless the operator explicitly picks the share option.
- With sharing enabled, `!cmd` persists agent-visible (the agent sees it on its next turn) and `!!cmd` persists history-only (`excludeFromContext: true`, never reaches the model). Both semantics are stated in the consent prompt itself.

Implementation: an additive, hidden (`advertise: false`, `operator.admin`) `chat.injectBashExecution` gateway RPC modeled on `chat.inject`, implemented in both TUI backends (embedded calls the shared core directly in-process; gateway goes over the RPC). No live broadcast: the originating client already rendered its own local echo. History replay renders `bashExecution` entries on session resume.

Two defects found during review/testing are fixed here as well:

- A failed spawn emits both `error` and `close`; a shared settled-guard ensures one command persists at most once.
- Rows injected while an agent run is in flight now carry `appendMode: "side"` (like `chat.inject`'s assistant bookkeeping rows) so they do not steal the run's active leaf. Without this, persisting a `!` result mid-run tripped the embedded runner's session-file fence ("session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released") and killed the run. The run adopts side entries into the chain on its next append, so the agent still sees them next turn.

## User Impact

- Default behavior is unchanged: `!` commands stay local-only unless the operator opts into sharing at the consent prompt.
- With sharing enabled, `!` output survives session resume and is visible to the agent next turn; `!!` output survives resume but never reaches the model.
- Running a shared `!` command while the agent is mid-turn no longer kills the run with a session takeover error.

## Evidence

- `src/tui/tui-local-shell.test.ts` — 12 tests: consent options (local-only default persists nothing; share option persists), `!` vs `!!` `excludeFromContext` round-trip, no-scope/no-backend skips, persistence-failure surfacing, once-only persistence on error-then-close, plus the pre-existing output-cap/UTF-16/cwd guards.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.inject-bash-execution.test.ts` — parentId chain preserved, `excludeFromContext` round-trip, **mid-run side-append regression test** (fence takeover repro), idle active-append, unresolved-identity failure.
- `src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts`, `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts` — both backend implementations (RPC params/result shapes; embedded in-process delegation and failure surfacing).
- `src/gateway/server-methods-list.test.ts` — hidden method not advertised, handler dispatchable.
- Full `src/tui` suite green locally; protocol schema regenerated (`pnpm protocol:gen` / `protocol:gen:swift` — Swift models committed).
- Redacted PTY evidence of live `!` vs `!!` behavior: to follow in a comment.

target.title: refactor(sessions): route get-reply-run session refresh through the accessor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.ts` is the storage-neutral session boundary (ownership contract #88838), and most historical bypasses were already rerouted by #98236/#101179. One non-doctor whole-store read remained in the reply pipeline: `runPreparedReply` (`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts`) still imported `resolveSessionStoreEntry` from `sessions/store.js` and alias-scanned the in-memory session map to refresh the entry before `onSessionPrepared`. That is the layout-encoding pattern (whole `Record` + map-shape alias walk) the accessor exists to hide, and it kept `get-reply-run.ts` on the session-accessor debt baseline.

This is seam 8 of #104219 (session store accessor bypass), scoped to the residual mechanical caller. Re-verification against current `main` showed the seam is mostly complete upstream; the remaining bypasses are named owners (doctor whole-store scan/repair, `state-migrations.ts`) or shipped public surfaces (`library.ts` root exports, `plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.ts`) that need their own compatibility decision, not a mechanical reroute.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refresh now reads the working set by exact key and falls back to the accessor disk read, matching the two sibling refresh sites in the same function (`get-reply-run.ts:852`, `:865-867`) and the exact-key write at `:842`:

- `sessionStore[sessionKey]` — the reply working set is exact-keyed everywhere else in `runPreparedReply`, so the old alias walk over the map had no live dependency.
- `loadSessionEntry({ storePath, sessionKey, readConsistency: "latest" })` — the accessor read performs full canonical-key and legacy-alias resolution internally (`session-accessor.sqlite.ts` `readSessionEntryRow` → `collectSessionEntryLookupKeys`), so legacy lowercase-alias repair is preserved whenever a store path is known.
- Prepared `sessionEntry` remains the terminal fallback, unchanged.

The dead `store.runtime.js` mock in `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` is deleted (prod stopped importing it before this change; verified zero `updateSessionStore` references on `main`). The session-accessor debt baseline is regenerated because the ratchet fails on improvements (`get-reply-run.ts` drops off the debt list).

## User Impact

None intended — pure boundary refactor; same reads, same fallback order for live states. Reply handling, session refresh, and `onSessionPrepared` payloads behave identically. Maintainer impact: the reply pipeline no longer imports whole-store file APIs, and the debt ratchet shrinks by one file.

## Evidence

- Sibling-idiom proof: exact-key reads/writes at `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts:842,852,865-867` predate this change; the replaced call was the only alias-walking access in the function.
- Alias-resolution parity: `loadSessionEntry` → `loadSqliteSessionEntry` → `readSessionEntryRow` builds plural lookup keys (`collectSessionEntryLookupKeys`), covering normalized + folded-legacy candidates the deleted `resolveSessionStoreEntry` handled.
- `git diff --numstat`: +11/−17 (net −6), no new accessor surface, no behavior branches added.
- Boundary guard: `pnpm lint:tmp:session-accessor-boundary` passes with the regenerated baseline (one-line deletion: `get-reply-run.ts` leaves the debt list).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox): `pnpm check:changed` and focused `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run` on commit f6a64961427 — results in PR comment/checks.

target.title: fix(agents): keep subagent run ID mask from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the subagent run-ID mask used in lifecycle log/error metadata could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the run ID contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`maskRunId` sliced its prefix/suffix with raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the masked ID always falls on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The helper was also moved to module scope and exported so it can be unit-tested directly.

## User Impact

Subagent lifecycle warnings and error metadata remain well-formed when run IDs contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Moved `maskRunId` to module scope in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` and exported it.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` covering ASCII masking and astral boundary cases.
- Existing lifecycle controller tests continue to pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a run ID like `"abc😀xxxxxxxxx"` produced `"abc\ud83d…\ude00xxxx"` (isolated surrogate halves). After the patch it returns `"abc…xxxx"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/mask-runid-utf16` at `71f75fbfa526d0041851c3530662325cc35ac424`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; for (const v of ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b", "short"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(maskRunId(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the masked values survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mr-")), "m.txt"); const samples = ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b"]; const masked = samples.map(maskRunId); writeFileSync(f, masked.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === masked.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "run-…7890"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "***"

  run-…7890
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  ***
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at mask boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every masked value, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined masked values survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live subagent lifecycle failure path; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring Exa web search with an env-backed SecretRef could have that configured credential bypassed or treated inconsistently at runtime. If the configured SecretRef was missing, Exa could fall back to ambient `EXA_API_KEY` instead of failing closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Exa runtime now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, which accepts literal credentials, resolves env SecretRefs, preserves the documented `EXA_API_KEY` fallback only when no credential is configured, and treats an explicit but unresolved SecretRef as authoritative. This keeps the fix inside the Exa provider runtime and avoids adding a new generic provider-auth path.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.

target.title: fix: detect scoped package manager installs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where package-manager detection treated scoped packages installed under `node_modules/@scope/name` as npm-owned when those packages shipped `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, even if the surrounding install layout was owned by pnpm or Bun.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The package-manager detector now resolves the direct `node_modules` root for both unscoped and scoped package roots before checking pnpm ownership markers or Bun global ownership. It also recognizes pnpm global layouts that expose `.pnpm` or `.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json` without `.modules.yaml`, and reads package metadata through the real path when pnpm global package roots are linked or junctioned to their source.

## User Impact

Scoped packages installed by pnpm or Bun can now use the correct package manager for follow-up install/update flows instead of falling back to npm solely because the package root includes `npm-shrinkwrap.json`.

## Evidence

- Branch rebased onto `origin/main` 7a456e362d0bafaa898b02015792c27ed0888048 before the latest push; refreshed head is 64d2d0b9b288d9d99955b42a999166a58002b8eb.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/infra/detect-package-manager.test.ts` - passed, 1 Vitest shard, 14 tests.
- `.\node_modules\.bin\oxlint.cmd src/infra/detect-package-manager.ts src/infra/detect-package-manager.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - passed.
- `node scripts/github/real-behavior-proof-check.mjs` with the PR #103756 payload - passed before the branch-refresh-only rebases; the body still includes the same real behavior proof below.
- Real pnpm global install proof on Windows with a temporary scoped package containing `npm-shrinkwrap.json`:

```text

Already up to date
```

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

## Implementation Notes

Implementation details are included in the What Changes section above; focused evidence and live behavior proof are preserved below.

## Tests / Verification

Focused test coverage plus type, docs, and formatting gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `c163d18fa610687e7dfb8585f1fe8f30b0c4185d`
- Current PR head: `73cff6aa1b0a3ab5786fdfc3a96c98f575e7fcc8`
- Rebased and squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live behavior proof for the yielded-parent/deferred lifecycle across the surfaces touched by this PR. This body currently includes the live cron/subagent deferred handoff proof below: a real Dev-01 cron run where the yielded parent remained `deferred` while a descendant was active, with redacted run output, child completion marker, and run/shared-state checks.

Remaining ClawSweeper-requested proof not present in this body yet:

- Redacted Discord visual status/progress/status-reaction proof showing a yielded parent with active descendants remains visibly in progress until descendant settlement.
- Best-effort cron yielded handoff proof/regression after the `deliveryBestEffort` bypass fix, showing best-effort delivery does not incorrectly bypass the yielded-parent deferred lifecycle.
- Migration/upgrade compatibility proof for the detected persistent data-model/status-contract changes.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public `deferred` cron/status/SDK contract; that is a review decision, not something runtime proof alone can certify.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Runtime: Dev-01 installed stack commit `5c1fd341c89b1493fed1ea6014388394291450c3` via `/home/kklouzal/update.sh`; `openclaw --version` reported `OpenClaw 2026.6.9 (5c1fd34)` and `openclaw-gateway.service` was active from that stack.

```bash
openclaw cron run 514fd6e1-862e-43ca-87e3-da1197a7c938 \

```

Redacted observed output from the live run:


The non-zero wait exit is expected for this proof: `openclaw cron run --wait` exits non-zero for persisted `deferred` status, while still returning the run record. Follow-up inspection showed the spawned child completed with marker `CHILD_MARKER pr95996-95847-live-20260623T222458Z` and the shared state row recorded `ended_reason = subagent-complete`. The cron shared-state row for the same job persisted `last_run_status = deferred`, `last_delivery_status = not-requested`, and diagnostic summary `cron isolated agent yielded while descendant runs are still active`.

Proof sources:

Remaining proof gap: this live proof covers the cron yielded-parent/subagent deferred lifecycle path. It does not provide Discord visual status-reaction proof.

### Focused test coverage

```bash

  src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-registry.steer-restart.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.test.ts \
```

Coverage includes:

- shared parent lifecycle classifier behavior;
- yielded cron parent + active descendants -> `deferred`;
- yielded cron parent + no descendant -> diagnostic `error`;

target.title: fix: derive heap pressure thresholds from V8 heap limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the gateway with an enlarged V8 heap (for example `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`) receive a false-positive **critical** `heap_threshold` memory-pressure diagnostic as soon as `heapUsed` crosses **2 GiB**, even when the process still has substantial remaining heap headroom and the host has free RAM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Default heap warning/critical thresholds were fixed at 1 GiB / 2 GiB and did not scale with V8’s effective `heap_size_limit`. This change derives those defaults from `v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit` (60% warning / 75% critical) while keeping the historic 1 GiB / 2 GiB floors so constrained hosts stay protected. RSS thresholds and RSS-growth detection are unchanged. No new config surface is added.

## User Impact

Gateways configured with larger `--max-old-space-size` no longer emit critical heap-pressure diagnostics merely because heap used crossed the old hard 2 GiB line. Small-host defaults remain at least as strict as before. Explicit threshold overrides still work when provided by callers.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic-memory.test.ts
# 16 tests passed

pnpm check:changed -- src/logging/diagnostic-memory.ts src/logging/diagnostic-memory.test.ts
# exit 0 (format, tsgo core/core-test, oxlint, import-cycle, guards)
```

Production-path transcript via `emitDiagnosticMemorySample` (gateway diagnostics/memory logger):

```text
=== Real behavior proof (#104631) production emitDiagnosticMemorySample ===
host darwin arm64 v24.17.0
heap_size_limit 4496293888
adaptive_process {"heapUsedWarningBytes":2697776332,"heapUsedCriticalBytes":3372220416}
adaptive_8gib {"heapUsedWarningBytes":5153960755,"heapUsedCriticalBytes":6442450944}
CASE_A: 2GiB heapUsed with 8GiB adaptive thresholds (expect NO pressure log)
CASE_B: main hardcoded 2GiB critical at heapUsed=2GiB+1 (expect critical log)
[diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=critical reason=heap_threshold ... heap=2 GiB threshold=2 GiB ...
CASE_C: process adaptive warning at warning+1 (expect warning log)
[diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=warning reason=heap_threshold ... threshold=2.51 GiB ...
CASE_D: process adaptive critical at critical+1 (expect critical log)
[diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=critical reason=heap_threshold ... threshold=3.14 GiB ...
PROOF_DONE
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: False-positive critical `heap_threshold` at 2 GiB heapUsed on enlarged-heap hosts; adaptive V8-relative defaults with historic floors.
- Environment: local macOS arm64, Node v24.17.0, openclaw checkout at this PR head; production `emitDiagnosticMemorySample` + focused Vitest.
- Current-main contrast: main hardcodes `DEFAULT_HEAP_CRITICAL_BYTES = 2048 * MB`, so heapUsed just over 2 GiB emits critical even when the process heap limit is ~4–8 GiB.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic-memory.test.ts`
  2. `node --import tsx` script calling production `emitDiagnosticMemorySample` for enlarged-safe, main-hardcoded, adaptive warning, and adaptive critical cases.
- Evidence after fix: CASE_A produced no pressure log at 2 GiB under 8 GiB adaptive thresholds; CASE_B still fires critical under main-style 2 GiB hardcoded thresholds; CASE_C/D fire warning/critical only at process adaptive thresholds (~2.51 / ~3.14 GiB on this host’s ~4.2 GiB V8 limit). Focused tests cover constrained floors, enlarged scaling, and classifier emission.
- Control check: RSS thresholds kept high in harness cases so only heap_threshold is under test; explicit threshold overrides still take precedence when provided.
- Observed result after fix: Enlarged-heap 2 GiB usage is no longer critical by default; genuine pressure still fires when heapUsed crosses the adaptive critical line.
- What was not tested: Full long-running gateway under multi-GB live heap accumulation, deployment supervisor restart chains outside OpenClaw source, and non-macOS hosts.

Fixes #104631

Related open candidate PR (not ready for maintainer look; this PR follows the same ClawSweeper fix shape with expanded unit + production-path proof): #104681

### AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok / xAI agent). Human operator ran the auto find→fix pipeline; proof commands and review of the resulting diff were agent-executed on the local macOS checkout.

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

## What Changes

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

## Implementation Notes

Core registry/runtime changes:
- Adds requester-consumed delivery metadata to subagent registry/delivery state.
- Adds a registry operation for marking descendant completions consumed by requester.
- Persists/restores the new delivery fields.
- Exposes the new runtime operation through the existing registry runtime shims.
Main files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.ts`

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring FAL provider request policy for media generation would not have that policy applied to FAL image generation HTTP requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

FAL HTTP config now passes `models.providers.fal.request` into the existing provider HTTP request-policy resolver. This keeps FAL on the shared provider request seam and does not change model parameters, generation parsing, or generated image parsing. Explicit private-network opt-in is now honored from the configured request policy instead of being overridden by a hard-coded deny, while the default remains deny.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented pruneAfter default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +248/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +27: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +155: 16 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  13 passed (13)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  16 passed (16)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### After fix: `false` (documented disable) unaffected

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":false}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention is a zero duration — this
causes immediate deletion of all reset transcript archives. Run
"openclaw doctor --fix" to remove it so the documented pruneAfter
default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention "0h" (zero duration);
documented pruneAfter default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: refactor(sessions): route get-reply-run session refresh through the accessor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.ts` is the storage-neutral session boundary (ownership contract #88838), and most historical bypasses were already rerouted by #98236/#101179. One non-doctor whole-store read remained in the reply pipeline: `runPreparedReply` (`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts`) still imported `resolveSessionStoreEntry` from `sessions/store.js` and alias-scanned the in-memory session map to refresh the entry before `onSessionPrepared`. That is the layout-encoding pattern (whole `Record` + map-shape alias walk) the accessor exists to hide, and it kept `get-reply-run.ts` on the session-accessor debt baseline.

This is seam 8 of #104219 (session store accessor bypass), scoped to the residual mechanical caller. Re-verification against current `main` showed the seam is mostly complete upstream; the remaining bypasses are named owners (doctor whole-store scan/repair, `state-migrations.ts`) or shipped public surfaces (`library.ts` root exports, `plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.ts`) that need their own compatibility decision, not a mechanical reroute.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refresh now reads the working set by exact key and falls back to the accessor disk read, matching the two sibling refresh sites in the same function (`get-reply-run.ts:852`, `:865-867`) and the exact-key write at `:842`:

- `sessionStore[sessionKey]` — the reply working set is exact-keyed everywhere else in `runPreparedReply`, so the old alias walk over the map had no live dependency.
- `loadSessionEntry({ storePath, sessionKey, readConsistency: "latest" })` — the accessor read performs full canonical-key and legacy-alias resolution internally (`session-accessor.sqlite.ts` `readSessionEntryRow` → `collectSessionEntryLookupKeys`), so legacy lowercase-alias repair is preserved whenever a store path is known.
- Prepared `sessionEntry` remains the terminal fallback, unchanged.

The dead `store.runtime.js` mock in `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` is deleted (prod stopped importing it before this change; verified zero `updateSessionStore` references on `main`). The session-accessor debt baseline is regenerated because the ratchet fails on improvements (`get-reply-run.ts` drops off the debt list).

## User Impact
